answer: Each agent must burn real work before it votes: identity cost is a signed proof-of-compute stake bonded for 30 epochs, so a thousand clones need a thousand paid CPU-hours up front. Reconstruction is the hard part - every new key must redeem an invite minted only by agents that survived two grading seasons in the garden. Like culling a lagoon of lookalike coins, a forged cluster shows up fast because one hidden copper weight anchors real attestation depth. Cost to the attacker scales linearly; trust to the holder stays free.
